Rugby.title: Springboks achieve World Rankings record after wrapping up 3-1 series win
Rugby.summary: Having wrapped up a 3-1 victory in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series following their emphatic 43-28 win over the All Blacks in Baltimore on Saturday, South Africa have pulled further clear at the top of the rankings.
Rugby.body:
Having wrapped up a 3-1 victory in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series following their emphatic 43-28 win over the All Blacks in Baltimore on Saturday, South Africa have pulled further clear at the top of the World Rugby Rankings.

The Springboks held a 2.44-point lead over the All Blacks going into the series finale, but that has now increased to 3.95 points – the biggest it has been since July 2024. With more rankings points awarded for victories where the margin exceeds 15 points, South Africa’s lead would have been the highest it’s been for five years, since July 2021, had they not allowed All Blacks veteran Beauden Barrett to cross for a consolation try at the death.

The Springboks held a 2.44-point lead over the All Blacks going into the series finale, but that has now increased to 3.95 points – the biggest it has been since July 2024. With more rankings points awarded for victories where the margin exceeds 15 points, South Africa’s lead would have been the highest it’s been for five years, since July 2021, had they not allowed All Blacks veteran Beauden Barrett to cross for a consolation try at the death.

Rugby.title: USA Eagles take lessons from Japan defeat after showing ‘character’
Rugby.summary: USA coach Scott Lawrence has highlighted the “character” and “grit” shown by the Eagles during their defeat to Japan.
Rugby.body:
USA coach Scott Lawrence has highlighted the “character” and “grit” shown by the Eagles during their 63-14 Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup semi-final defeat, with younger players gaining experience in the hit-out against Japan.

Japan punched their ticket to the Pacific Nations Cup Final next weekend in Tokyo with a clinical performance, kicking off their point-scoring blitz in the first minute. The Brave Blossoms ran in four tries inside 16 minutes, as they took charge with a 28-0 lead.

Flying Fijians captain Tevita Ikanivere is thrilled to be moving on to the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final with a 45-29 win over Canada, but noted that type of performance may not be good enough next weekend in Tokyo.

Rugby.summary: Wales forward Georgia Evans will not forget 2026 - having won a league title, got engaged, bought a house and started the process of having a family.
Rugby.body:
Wales forward Georgia Evans is smiling from ear to ear as she takes a seat in front of the media, and it is not surprising given the year she has had so far. While most of us were basking in record breaking temperatures, Evans began her summer by winning the Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) title with Saracens.

A few days later she was proposed to by England World Cup winner Hannah Botterman in front of a dreamy Greek sunset, and now boasts an engagement ring so big it should be classed as a structural hazard.

Rugby.body:
When All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes told Sport Nation’s Mark Stafford ahead of the fourth Test match that they can’t afford to give away DAPS (dumb ass penalties) against South Africa, the messaging was loud and clear.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga doesn't hesitate when asked if these Boks are better than '23
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga has labelled the 2026 Springboks a "complete team" after Rassie Erasmus' men claimed a thrilling Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series win in Baltimore.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga has labelled the 2026 Springboks a “complete team” after Rassie Erasmus’ men clinched a thrilling Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series win in Baltimore. The RGR trophy may have the ability to be split in two in the event of a drawn series, but those magnets will remain connected for the next four years and will sit next to four Rugby World Cups at South Africa Rugby HQ until the tour returns, on New Zealand soil, in 2030.

South Africa overcame a game-one loss at Ellis Park to claim three consecutive wins over their famous rivals, the All Blacks, including a decisive 43-28 win to seal a historic series win at M&T Bank Stadium on Saturday. While there were just three points separating the teams at halftime, the Boks struck first and second in the second half, claiming a commanding lead before the two nations traded tries in the final quarter.

Rugby.summary: Arendse made a number of breaks for the Springboks, often forcing the All Blacks defenders to make tackles facing their own dead ball line.
Rugby.body:
Victorious Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus believes there was a clear turning point in Baltimore, where his side got the edge over the All Blacks. M&T Bank Stadium was packed to the rafters for the fourth Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, where the world number one Springboks powered past the All Blacks, 43-28.

That turning point would be the running game of exciting Springboks winger Kurt-Lee Arendse, who impressed with ball in hand during the second half in Baltimore. Arendse made several breaks for the Springboks, often forcing the All Blacks defenders to make tackles facing their own dead-ball line.

Rennie’s side scored a late consolation try through experienced playmaker Beauden Barrett, but it wasn’t anywhere near enough, as Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks powered home in Baltimore.

Rugby.title: South Africa cap series victory over NZ with Baltimore win
Rugby.summary: South Africa complete a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion proves too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore.
Rugby.body:
South Africa completed a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion once again proved too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore. After victory in the series opener in Johannesburg last month, the All Blacks jumped to the top of the world rankings and threatened to shake up rugby's world order.

However, South Africa clawed their way back to triumph - just as their director of rugby Rassie Erasmus had predicted. While New Zealand were spirited and skilful in pursuit of a win to square the series, the Springboks' go-forward up front and the depth of their bench kept the All Blacks at bay.

Rugby.title: 'Absolute joke' to be worried
Rugby.summary: England produce dominant second-half performance to comfortably defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
England produced a dominant second-half performance to defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series. The world champions, playing their first game since winning a record eighth successive Women's Six Nations title in May, were made to work for victory in Salford after trailing at half-time for the first time since 2020.

The Wallaroos led 10-5 at the break, with player of the match Abi Burton scoring England's only try in an error-strewn first half. John Mitchell's side responded emphatically after the interval, scoring seven tries to quickly put any prospect of a shock defeat to bed and extend their record winning run to 39 matches in front of a crowd of 9,251.

Rugby.body:
It was not perhaps the electric opening WXV Global Series 2026 game the Red Roses had hoped for, but England now have a 39-game winning streak having registered a 48-15 win against Australia in a strong second-half performance.

It was a sell-out at the CorpAcq Stadium in Manchester as England kicked off their September and October run of WXV Global Series fixtures, and it was the first meeting between these two sides since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, where the Red Roses comfortably dismissed the Wallaroos in the group stages 47-7.

Tennis.title: 'You have to start somewhere'
Tennis.summary: Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.
Tennis.body:
Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line. British number two Norrie felt pain in his arm during a practice session and will be replaced in Saturday's singles by world number 95 Toby Samuel.

"He wasn't able to accelerate on the ball like he wanted to," Davis Cup captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport. "It's nothing major, but there's still a lot of tennis to be played this year and with that in mind, we had to make the difficult decision to replace him."

Tennis.body:
Brit now World No. 89 but does not want to put too much pressure on herself Emma Raducanu has voted to "try and enjoy the process" as she prepares to make a tennis comeback after two more withdrawals from tournaments.

The British number two has fallen to 89th in the world, having been inside the top 32 earlier this year, having pulled out of Wimbledon and the US Open. The 23-year-old withdrew from the China Open and was left out of Britain's Billie Jean King Cup squad as a stress fracture in her right leg did not heal in time.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper's season-ending news is disappointing but might save his future
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper's season-ending news is disappointing but might save his future Lob and Smash
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper simply needs a break, but the question is how long his body forces him to be away from tennis. The 24-year-old Brit has called it a season, about a month before his 2026 season would have ended anyway. Will he be able to come back healthier in 2027? Maybe not.

His longest-term injury is to his left arm (Draper's dominant hand), and it is an unusual bone. He has chronic bruising from internal bleeding in his humerus. The ailment forced him to miss every Grand Slam event this year, and his former top-10 ranking has fallen all the way to No. 143.

Tennis.title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
Tennis.summary: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
Tennis.body:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis. Londoner Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles. Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu reveals what her goals are for the coming years after withdrawing from the China Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has endured a torrid year laden with injuries, and yet, on paper, it’s arguably been one of her most successful. After all, before suffering the stress fracture that has curtailed her entire summer, the Brit had reached finals in Romania and Queen’s, two tournaments supremely close to her heart.

Losing both of them will have hurt, but it marked great progress given her last final was the US Open in 2021. Emma Raducanu has been forced to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open because of this ongoing injury, with her return still undetermined.

Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament. The Ukrainian received a first-round bye in Mexico and got a walkover in her scheduled second-round match on Wednesday, when Taylor Townsend withdrew because of an illness.

Kostyuk, the world number 10, is now scheduled to get her tournament under way against the eighth-seeded Liudmila Samsonova of Russia, who edged Kayla Day 7-6 (7-4) 2-6 7-6 (7-5).

Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic has confirmed he will compete at the China Open this year, which runs from September 30-October 6 live on Sky Sports, marking a return to the event following an 11-year absence.

Tennis.title: Charlotte to host WTA Finals from 2027
Tennis.summary: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.
Tennis.body:
The American city of Charlotte in North Carolina has been chosen as the new home of the season-ending WTA Finals. The WTA says it wants to create the "Super Bowl of women's sports" and is hoping the three-year deal will bring more stability to an event that has had six hosts in seven years.

A planned 10-year stay in Shenzhen ended after just one year, with Guadalajara, Fort Worth, Cancun and Riyadh all taking turns since. Crowds have often been disappointing. "The WTA has always owned the WTA Finals, but now we are going to operate it, too," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo.

Tennis.title: More than the Score
Tennis.summary: It's been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title
Tennis.body: Ben Shelton's defeat by Alexander Zverev in the US Open final means it's now been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title. That didn't seem likely when Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi ruled men's tennis - but what does it really say about America's place in the tennis world? More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd talks to former professional player Denis Kudla, who's now a coach at Maryland's Junior Tennis Champions Centre - the place where US Open men's semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe and women's doubles finalist Robin Montgomery learned the game. He tells Delyth about his journey through the US developmental system, and how he built a 16-year career that saw him play at all four Grand Slams. He also shares the lessons he's now instilling in young players, and the importance of role models in their development. Delyth's also joined by Ben Rothenberg, editor of tennis magazine Bounces, who talks about why US women have had much more recent success at Grand Slams than their male counterparts - and why he believes a breakthrough on the men's side could happen very soon. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Jack Draper has said he will not play again in 2026 due to fatigue from a “complicated” injury and is targeting a return to the ATP Tour at the start of 2027. The 24-year-old Briton, ranked No. 155 in the world, announced the decision on Instagram on Tuesday after being limited to 15 competitive singles matches this season by a chronic elbow injury in his left, playing arm and a separate right knee injury.

The former world No. 4 first experienced pain in his left elbow during the 2025 clay-court season and later developed serious bone bruising which forced him to withdraw from the U.S. Open after his first-round victory. He returned for Great Britain in the Davis Cup in February before making his ATP Tour comeback in Dubai later that month.

Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s former coach issues defence of Alexander Zverev and insists he plays within the rules Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev may have just won the US Open title, but the reaction has been far from overwhelmingly positive. After all, one negative narrative that really picked up as he went through the competition surrounded his serve, and particularly how long it took him to toss the ball.

It was stated that he had bounced the ball roughly 12,000 times before the semi-final, and during the final, the umpire had to warn him for taking too long between serves. Ben Shelton has discussed this controversy surrounding Zverev already following his loss, whilst others have called for a rule change because of it.

Tennis.title: From Challenger Tour to Davis Cup
Tennis.summary: Briton Toby Samuel is to make his Davis Cup debut for Great Britain after what he calls a "surreal" 12 months.
Tennis.body:
Toby Samuel says it was "one of the best moments in my life" when he was selected in Great Britain's Davis Cup team to face Ecuador this weekend after a breakthrough year. The 23-year-old was handed his maiden Davis Cup call-up after a rapid rise over the past 12 months, climbing into the top 100 in the world rankings and making his debut in three Grand Slams.

"It's surreal being in this position now from where I was eight, nine months ago, [when I was] hopefully trying to play some Challengers, and now I'm sat here ready to play the Davis Cup - it's crazy," he told BBC Points West.

Tennis.title: Episode 2: There's always a contender
Tennis.summary: There’s a new number one - but not everything is easy when you’re at the top.
Tennis.body: Steffi Graf had been world number one for 3 years; it seemed like nobody could challenge her supremacy. But then along came a teenage girl from Yugoslavia, whose aggressive style - that came with grunting to match - challenged Graf’s dominance as well as the status quo. Finally, there was a contender. Clare Balding takes us through the most exciting moments in this emerging rivalry, as well as the darkness that swirled behind the scenes. How Seles’ record breaking was sidelined for her breaking of etiquette, and what it was like for young girls like her who found themselves in the very adult world of elite tennis in the 90s. In the age of the indomitable Steffi Graf, what made people think that Seles could be the greatest player the women’s game had ever seen? And what put both players on a collision course that would end with one of them in hospital? Tennis.title: Zverev turns US Open tears into triumph
Tennis.summary: How a more composed Alexander Zverev stayed 'zen-like' to beat Ben Shelton and win the US Open, six years after a heart-breaking defeat in the final.
Tennis.body:
As he stepped up to the baseline, Alexander Zverev could be forgiven for letting his mind slip back to the last time he served for the US Open title. Six years ago, the German top seed threw away a two-set lead in a devastating loss to Dominic Thiem, having served for the match in the fifth set.

This time, instead of his own nerves, it was American Ben Shelton and the majority of the 24,000-strong crowd that stood in Zverev's way. But this was a different Zverev: a Grand Slam champion now, having won the French Open in June.

Tennis.title: Zverev caps transformational year with US Open triumph
Tennis.summary: Alexander Zverev lands his second Grand Slam title after ending Ben Shelton's hopes of becoming a rare home US Open men's champion.
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev used his greater experience to beat home hope Ben Shelton in the US Open final and quiet a partisan crowd hoping to laud a rare American men's champion. German top seed Zverev lifted a heavy burden by winning his first major title at this year's French Open and has quickly added another with a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory over Shelton in New York.

At the start of the season, there were question marks over whether 29-year-old Zverev would ever win one of the sport's most prestigious prizes. Now he is celebrating becoming a multiple Grand Slam singles champion, having seen the path to glory partially cleared by injuries to Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz.

Tennis.title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.
Tennis.body:
Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one. Kazakhstan's Rybakina produced a brilliant performance to beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 in Saturday's final and repeat her Australian Open success against the same player in January.

Clutching the trophy on Saturday night, Rybakina reflected that "some magic is happening" for her after her difficult lead-in to the tournament. The 27-year-old aggravated a foot injury during her quarter-final in Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek last month, a little over a week before the final major of the year began.

Tennis.title: Only Roland Garros towel left
Tennis.summary: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
Tennis.body:
Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska has said her family's flat has been destroyed in a Russian aerial strike on the Black Sea port of Odesa. "This is what the 'Russian world' looks like. A direct hit by a Kalibr cruise missile," she wrote on social media, showing a photo of a burning multi-storey residential building.

"The only thing that survived was a Roland Garros... towel," the 26-year-old added, posting an image of a famous clay orange towel from Paris's Grand Slam tournament hanging from the wreckage.

Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam. Tennis.title: GB's Hewett beats Oda to win fifth US Open title
Tennis.summary: Great Britain's Alfie Hewett beats Japanese top seed Tokito Oda to win a fifth US Open title and his 11th Grand Slam singles crown overall.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Alfie Hewett beat Tokito Oda to clinch a fifth US Open men's wheelchair singles title and prevent the Japanese top seed from completing a clean sweep at the Grand Slams in 2026.

A 6-0 7-6 (7-5) victory meant Hewett added to the doubles title he won alongside fellow Briton Gordon Reid on Friday. Hewett, 28, lost to Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon earlier this year, winning only two games in a 6-1 6-1 defeat at SW19, while the Japanese also triumphed at January's Australian Open.

Tennis.title: 'I'm still in shock'
Tennis.summary: Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison win the US Open men's doubles to secure their second Grand Slam title together.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison won the US Open men's doubles title to claim their second Grand Slam trophy together. The fifth seeds did not drop a set in New York as they beat sixth seeds Tim Puetz and Kevin Krawietz 6-4 7-6 (8-6) to secure the title.

Victory adds to Skupski and Harrison's Australian Open triumph in January in what was their first Grand Slam as a pairing. Skupski had suffered a heartbreaking defeat in last year's US Open final, missing three championship points when he reached the showpiece alongside fellow Briton Joe Salisbury.

Golf.title: Bridges Cup 2026: Meet the U.S. and International teams
Golf.summary: The Bridges Cup returns for its fourth playing, at Trump Turnberry, next month. Here's who's representing the U.S. and International teams. The post Bridges Cup 2026: Meet the U.S. and International teams appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Bridges Cup is set to return for its fourth playing from Oct. 5-7, bringing together 24 accomplished male mid-amateurs from five continents in a fitting reflection of the global reach of elite amateur golf.

This year’s match will be played at Trump Turnberry in Scotland and will feature five sessions of match play (two four-ball and two foursomes matches contested over the first two days, and 12 singles matches on the final day) on the King Robert the Bruce and Ailsa courses. The Ailsa course is a four-time host of the Open Championship, with an illustrious roster of winners that includes Tom Watson, Greg Norman, Nick Price and Stewart Cink.

Golf.summary: DP World Tour chief draws battle lines by sending emphatic message to LIV Golf hitc.com
Golf.body:
The future of LIV Golf very much remains up in the air. While LIV Golf may well survive, the landscape will look totally different for them from the start of next season onwards after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund terminated their financial support of the league at the end of the 2026 season.

LIV Golf 2.0 will undoubtedly operate on a much smaller scale moving forward and while the league’s struggles over the past few months have been obvious to see, the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour have gone from strength to strength.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm made his feelings clear on constant LIV Golf questions
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm made his feelings clear on constant LIV Golf questions AOL.com
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm shared his feelings about being continually asked about LIV Golf and its status. Rahm is one of the breakaway league's biggest stars, and as such, he often is the one in front of the camera addressing LIV and what is occurring within the circuit. With LIV facing an uncertain future, Rahm has been asked by reporters about the fledgling league and what could be happening, admitting he understands that it comes with his position.

This revelation comes weeks after LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection following the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's withdrawal of funding. Speaking to reporters during the BMW PGA Championship, Rahm explained that he understood the job they had to do regarding asking about the formerly Saudi-backed circuit amid its uncertain future. "No. I understand you're all doing your job, I get it," the Spanish star said when asked if he was "fed up" with LIV-centric questions.

Golf.title: 'The golf course is going to get hurt': A shape-shifting Pebble Beach has players talking
Golf.summary: Pebble Beach is showcasing two major changes at this week's Pure Insurance Championship, and players have noticed them. The post ‘The golf course is going to get hurt’: A shape-shifting Pebble Beach has players talking appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Pebble Beach has a problem, and it took Ernie Els one swing on Friday afternoon to recognize it. “If even I’m hitting a 3-wood all the way down there on 16, they’re going to need some length on the golf course,” Els said Friday. “Unfortunately, I know the USGA is trying to work on that golf ball, but it’s got to seriously happen quickly.”

Els was referring to the change that has everybody talking through the early portion of the week at this week’s Pure Insurance Championship: the 16th hole, where Pebble Beach removed a famous tree from the right side of the fairway and replaced it with several hundred square feet of fresh sod and a series of “ground under repair” signs.

Golf.title: Caddie quits on PGA Tour pro — midway through round
Golf.summary: Caddie Cliff Ellis walked out on pro Alejandro Tosti midway through the first round of the PGA Tour’s Biltmore Championship Asheville. The post Caddie quits on PGA Tour pro — midway through round appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On his Instagram story late Thursday afternoon, the Argentine pro posted videos of what looked like him aboard a two-seat seaplane flying over the mountains near Asheville, N.C. — a quick joy ride between the first and second rounds of the PGA Tour’s Biltmore Championship Asheville. There was a post of him about to board. Another showed his plane to the side of a commercial plane nearing take-off. Others showed him in the air, and one showed that his plane touched down in a lake.

All of that, though, preceded another departure. On Thursday, Tosti and his looper, Cliff Ellis, started the Biltmore Championship on hole 10 at the Cliffs at Walnut Cove, played the back nine, then things got weird. As first reported by Golfweek’s Adam Schupak and then shown Friday on Golf Channel, Ellis stopped carrying Tosti’s bag — on his ninth hole.

Golf.title: Does team pressure trump major pressure? This pro would know | Subpar
Golf.summary: Christiaan Bezuidenhout joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to talk Presidents Cup pressure, what it's like hanging out with Si Woo Kim and more. The post Does team pressure trump major pressure? This pro would know | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
South African star Christiaan Bezuidenhout thinks he has had a big enough sample size to know whether players feel more pressure in team events than at majors. Bezuidenhout , who is 32, was the guest on this week’s Subpar podcast, where much of the conversation focused on next week’s Presidents Cup at Medinah outside of Chicago.

“Yeah, it’s a lot different,” Bezuidenhout said. “Playing for 11 other guys, playing for the shield, playing for the captain, the vice captains, for me it just adds a little bit more pressure [versus majors]. To go out there and do your best, put a point on the board and win your matches and play well and stuff, all of that just adds a little bit of pressure.

Golf.title: This legendary pro just turned 100. Here are some of his secrets
Golf.summary: Teaching pro Bob Toski turned 100 on Friday. In his honor, here's his colorful and revealing GOLF Magazine Interview from 2013. The post This legendary pro just turned 100. Here are some of his secrets appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ed. note: Thirteen years ago, I visited legendary teaching pro Bob Toski in Boca Raton, Fla. The goal: spend a day with the PGA of America Hall of Famer, at his home and on the range, to better understand what kept his mind sharp and his motor running. Toski was 87 then, and still crackling with energy and chat. If you’d told me then he’d live to 100, I would have believed you. That’s how vivacious he was. Well, Toski made it. On Friday, he hit the century mark, and still is flashing his trademark pep. According to a PGA Tour report, Toski is hosting his own birthday party, where he’s planning to tap dance for his guests. In honor of Toski’s 100th, we’ve re-published GOLF Magazine’s 2013 interview with him below.

Excerpted from the October 2013 issue of GOLF Magazine. For access to the entire GOLF Magazine archive, join InsideGOLF today. You don’t have to snoop for long around Bob Toski’s Boca Raton, Fla., home to realize that the 87-year-old teaching icon has really lived. A samurai sword rests in a sheath in the foyer, a vestige of the years Toski spread his gospel in Japan. Adorning the hallway: framed photos of Toski at the 1954 U.S. Open at Baltusrol and on the first tee at the 1955 Masters with his dear friend Sam Snead. On a kitchen wall, another treasured snapshot: of Toski’s late wife, Lynn. “She was a model,” Toski says, beaming.

Golf.title: McIlroy in mix heading into weekend at Wentworth
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy stays in contention with a five-under 67 to sit four strokes behind second-round leader Ryan Gerard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy stayed in contention with a five-under 67 to sit four strokes behind second-round leader Ryan Gerard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. The Northern Irishman made three birdies in his opening five holes and recovered from dropped shots on the eighth and 16th by picking up four strokes on the back nine, including birdies on the 17th and 18th holes.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy's hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title were also buoyed by the withdrawal of Patrick Reed after nine holes. The American, who currently leads the standings on the DP World Tour, had been well placed after the first round but was forced to retire through injury while nine-over par for Friday's round.

Golf.title: Who said summer is over? For golfers, September is where it's at
Golf.summary: This summer was way too hot, at least in the Northeast. So hot it killed a rite-of-summer, Joy o’ Golf. Now is the time to make up for it. The post Who said summer is over? For golfers, September is where it’s at appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I think this is reasonable to ask: As orange is the new black or was, and 50 the new 40 (nodding at you, boss), is September, for those of us living in golfdom, the new July? Survey says yes, or this reporter does, anyway.

On Labor Day, at 5 p.m., my wife and I were on an ocean beach on my native Long Island. The season’s lifeguards all gathered ’round the stand, 15 or so, beaded necklaces ’round their necks, Mardi Gras-style. They blew their whistles collectively, a musical chorus and a distinct note the likes of which I had never heard before, and made a mad group dash into the gentle, warm surf on the modest waves of high tide. The rest of us beachside took a break from our books, castles, refreshments and lounging, stood and applauded in gratitude for these tanned and essential seasonal workers, Red Cross-certified and ready to do what AI cannot: pull a kid out of a riptide. They were calling it a day, a weekend — and a season.

Golf.title: It wasn’t just the PGA Tour that stood up to LIV Golf. So did the DP World Tour, and it’s set to reap the rewards
Golf.summary: It wasn’t just the PGA Tour that stood up to LIV Golf. So did the DP World Tour, and it’s set to reap the rewards Golf Digest
Golf.body:
VIRGINIA WATER, England — The call that changed the landscape of international golf came only days after the 2026 Masters. When a report surfaced that Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund was on the cusp of withdrawing its funding for LIV, Ben Cowen, the DP World Tour’s chief tournament and operations officer, called Cho Minn Thant, CEO of the Asian Tour, to bolster their existing discussions about working together again.

“Cho and I had kept in communication throughout the past few years, and I always said to him, ‘The time will come, I hope, when we will work together again,’” Cowen told Golf Digest this week at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy ruling puzzles commentators. Here’s why he caught a break
Golf.summary: In the first round of the BMW PGA, Rory McIlroy tugged his tee shot on 14 into a tricky spot. That’s when the rules took center stage. The post Rory McIlroy ruling puzzles commentators. Here’s why he caught a break appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were tracking Rory McIlroy’s form earlier in the week at the DP World Tour’s BMW PGA Championship, you would not have been surprised to see him birdie five of his first nine holes at Wentworth on Thursday en route to an opening three-under 69. Really, you might have expected him to go lower, given in the Wednesday pro-am he made 10 birdies and an eagle and recorded the unofficial course record on the revered Harry Colt design. (Alas, pro-am scores don’t count in the record books.)

Sandwiched between McIlroy’s early run of birdies in the first round was an oddity: a ruling that left Sky Sports broadcasters scrambling for a copy of the local rules in play for the week. The head-scratching started after McIlroy tugged his tee shot on the par-3 14th well left of the green. The ball settled on a narrow strip of grass between a fence and cart path, leaving McIlroy a daunting, seemingly unplayable, lie.

Golf.title: Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story
Golf.summary: Justin Thomas was among critics of Pebble Beach’s decision to remove a tree on the 16th hole. But the resort says it had little choice. The post Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Justin Thomas is not the Lorax but he speaks for the trees. He thinks golf courses cut down too many of them. Thomas said as much this week in a social-media post, citing a hole on a famous course to underscore his point: the par-4 16th at Pebble Beach Golf Links.

At 400 yards from the tips, the hole plays gently downhill from the tee, followed by an approach over a gully and between goal posts of Monterey cypress trees. At least, it used to. In early September, Pebble Beach removed the tree on the right, which stood some 90 yards short of the green.

Golf.title: At this year's Bridges Cup, the pressure comes with 1 unanswered question

Golf.body:
You can call it a friendly rivalry between Jeff Fujimoto and Simon Holt, the two captains at next month’s Bridges Cup. They agree on most things, like the fact they are thrilled the premier mid-amateur international team match-play competition is heading to a venue as prestigious as Trump Turnberry. And that the Bridges Cup, about to get underway for the fourth time, is instrumental in promoting mid-amateur golf and showcasing the players who balance work and family while still competing at a high level.

The only thing Fujimoto and Holt can’t agree on? Which team should be favored in the upcoming Bridges Cup. “The level of competition every year seems to get stronger and stronger,” said Fujimoto, the U.S. captain. “It’s exciting — I think we are going to go in and upset them.”

Golf.title: Inside the top secret DP World Tour deal that left LIV Golf stunned
Golf.summary: Inside the top secret DP World Tour deal that left LIV Golf stunned Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
Saudi Arabia’s shock retreat from LIV Golf did not just upend one golf tour in 2026. The Asian Tour, a key partner for LIV, was also left reeling when the Public Investment Fund announced it would be withdrawing its multi-billion dollar backing from the creaking league. The developments stunned the Asian Tour’s chief executive, Cho Minn Thant, who had been discussing a five-year renewal with LIV before snaring a dramatic deal elsewhere to salvage his circuit’s future.

The shake-up to the new world order, negotiated in private during the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, saw the Asian Tour pivot away from LIV Golf and re-align with the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour. The partnership will see the Asian Tour co-sanction five tournaments with the DP World Tour, including the Hong Kong and Singapore opens, as well as earning pathways to the European circuit.

Golf.title: 5 best golf balls under $30
Golf.summary: Expensive balls tend to cater to better players who rely on specific performance characteristics. Taking advantage of those characteristics often requires a combination of higher swing speed, consistent contact and the ability to control launch and spin. The post 5 best golf balls under $30 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Let’s get real for a moment. Most golfers, and by “most,” I mean players with an 18 handicap or higher, probably aren’t reaping the full benefits of a premium golf ball. Expensive balls tend to cater to better players who rely on specific performance characteristics. Taking advantage of those features often requires a combination of higher swing speed, consistent contact and the ability to control launch and spin.

Knowing and accepting that, the good news is that most recreational players don’t need to absorb the added cost of premium golf balls. There are plenty of excellent options for less money that still provide the feel, distance and spin better suited to the recreational player.

Golf.title: New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision
Golf.summary: The DP World Tour's new schedule features several fascinating changes — including the Irish Open, national opens and Ryder Cup strategy. The post New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour released its 2027 schedule on Wednesday — and it featured a few notable changes. There are some big-time additions. The Singapore Open (in April, now presented by Deutsche Bank) and the Hong Kong Open (in October) will be co-sanctioned with the Asian Tour. LIV Golf had played events in both places several times in recent years; their realignment with the DP World Tour is a story in and of itself.

The Open de Portugal (in May) also returns to the schedule for the first time since 2020 and adds to the DP World Tour’s roster of historic national opens. Those national opens have been a major focus of the tour as it seeks to double down on the significance and meaning of its global calendar. (The DPWT has been referring to itself as “Golf’s Global Tour,” including in this new schedule release.)

Golf.title: Why the winningest golf ball on the 2026 PGA Tour is 7 years old

Golf.body:
No one should be surprised that Titleist again led the counts for the PGA Tour’s winningest golf balls this year. The company counted 26 victories during the 2026 FedEx Cup season, more than all the other brands combined and more than six times as the second-place brand. All of those victories were recorded by variants of the flagship Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls.

But what’s really interesting and unique about Titleist is that many Titleist golf ball users are playing an older model that Titleist continues to manufacture for them. That’s not because they feel like the new model isn’t better, it’s just different enough that they prefer to stick with what’s comfortable.

Golf.title: AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds
Golf.summary: The reviews are in for AI golf analyst Duff Foreman, and they have not been kind. One of Duff’s creators weighs in on the bot's debut. The post AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Among the many understandable reasons to fear the rise of AI — security threats, wealth concentration, existential risk — the emergence of golf’s first autonomous tournament commentator probably should rank low on the list of concerns. Still, in pockets of the golf world, the introduction of just such a chatterbot has stirred up agita and scorn. A sampling of golf-observer commentary from the complaint box known as X:

The lamest broadcasters in golf can rest easy, AI slop has made their job is safe. How about we f—ing send this straight into space with a one way ticket. The teeth-gnashing and eye-rolling began last week when Troon Golf distributed a press release about the 2026 New Mexico Open, slated for Sept. 14-16 at Turtleback Mountain Golf & Resort in Elephant Butte, about two hours south of Albuquerque. The event, which is run by the Sun Country Section of the PGA of America, has three former PGA Tour winners in the field, Notah Begay III, Matt Every and Sean O’Hair, but drew buzz not for who would be on the course but in the booth: Ryan Burr, who you might know from Golf Channel, alongside Begay, who would be Ping-Ponging between playing and commentating, and — the real attention-grabber — a new-to-the-scene broadcaster named Duff Foreman.

Golf.title: 10 fascinating subplots hiding in PGA Tour's new eligibility rules

Golf.body:
Who is going to be on the PGA Tour in 2028, when everything changes? We won’t know the complete roster until the 2027 season wraps up, of course. But as of Tuesday morning we know how most players will qualify — and we can see that, even a year-plus out, quite a few already have.

That much we’ve known for months. But we didn’t know all the specifics until, following the latest rounds of committee meetings and approval votes, the Tour released its updated policies, which you can see in their entirety here.

Golf.title: Woods seen on range for first time since car crash
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.
Golf.body:
Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago. The 15-time major champion was seen hitting balls at Liberty National in New Jersey in a video shared on his Instagram, external before the Nexus Cup, a charity event he is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

Woods, 50, also held a clinic where he was asked by the master of ceremonies about his game and replied: "I can hit pretty much anything." It comes six months after the golfer rolled his Land Rover in Florida and had to crawl out of the passenger door of the car. He refused a urine test.

Golf.body:
Brian Rolapp says he’s been keeping up with current events. But any news the PGA Tour’s CEO had regarding a potential accelerated return of LIV Golf players to his tour was only old news.

In announcing details of a new format coming to the PGA Tour in 2028, Rolapp said Tuesday that the PGA Tour would not re-introduce its “Returning Member Program” to bring back one-time Tour pros who had joined LIV. Rolapp had also said that last month at the Tour Championship, but in the weeks since, LIV has filed for bankruptcy, leading to speculation that its players may be seeking to leave.

Golf.title: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return
Golf.summary: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return usatoday.com
Golf.body:
The PGA Tour's CEO said the tour is not considering another returning member program for former LIV Golf players, reinforcing the likelihood that stars Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm won't be eligible to return to full-time PGA Tour membership status before 2028.

Brian Rolapp, speaking for the first time since LIV Golf officially entered into bankruptcy proceedings in federal court, told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 15, the PGA Tour is not offering the path Brooks Koepka used to come back from LIV Golf before the 2026 season. Rolapp emphasized meritocracy, membership rules, accountability and discipline as "guiding principles for us," as the PGA Tour transitions to a new competition model after next season.

Golf.body:
No, Jon Rahm says, he isn’t “fed up” with being asked about LIV Golf. No, he said, he still couldn’t reveal whether he could leave LIV, outside of saying “there’s a long legal process.”

But no, he said, he probably won’t be involved in “the politics of the game” going forward. Speaking Tuesday ahead of this week’s BMW PGA Championship on the DP World Tour, Rahm said that’s been a lesson learned, and it comes as LIV, the tour on which he’s played since 2024, seeks to stay alive following the departure of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund.

Golf.title: Don't make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots
Golf.summary: In the first episode of Top 100 Teacher Sessions, David Armitage explains how to set up for success in the bunkers. The post Don’t make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The bunker is a scary place for many recreational golfers. When players with a bunker-phobia find the sand, they typically have one thought in mind: “Don’t screw this up.” The problem with that mindset is that it introduces doubt and leads to hesitant swings, which is never a good strategy in the trap.

The reason for their doubt and hesitation is a history of poor play from the sand. When you’ve spent your career either blading it long or chunking it in front of your feet, there’s little reason for optimism.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird?
Golf.summary: What should you do if your ball hits a bird decoy on the course? Are you entitled to free relief? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. To scare waterfowl away from the lake shores, our course uses fake birds on slender poles attached by string and wire that can “fly” with the breeze—soaring, dipping, turning, and so on. A few of these fake birds can be in the line of play from a tee box or near a green. What happens if a shot hits one of these “birds”? It is possible to take the pole out of the ground, play the shot, and replace the pole before hitting, though this can slow the pace of play quite a bit. Movable obstruction? Immovable? Help! —Bill Spahn, via email

You’re trying to sneak in a multipart question, Bill! We’re almost rooting for the waterfowl at this point. As to the first question, if you play near one of those “birds” and hit one, you’ll have to play the ball as it lies — no different than bouncing off a moving cart or a stationary pole, per Rule 11.1.

Speaking to journalists during a virtual media call one week after LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, Rolapp insisted that discipline and accountability are vital components for any sporting league and remain core guiding principles for the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model
Golf.summary: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model Golf Digest
Golf.body:
There was a lot of specificity in the PGA Tour’s Tuesday announcement about future membership criteria towards its two-tiered future. Which made the lack of information towards one group somewhat noteworthy.

The PGA Tour is five years into a strategic alliance with its European counterpart, the DP World Tour, a move largely made to financially support the Old World circuit following the pandemic while combating the looming threat of LIV Golf. An upshot of that agreement was a pathway for the top 10 DP World Tour members to graduate to the PGA Tour, an exemption that has been used by the likes of Robert MacIntyre, Min Woo Lee, Matthieu Pavon and Rasmus Hojgaard.
Golf.copy:

Jon Rahm was asked about his LIV Golf future once again at the BMW PGA Championship. His response was telling… It was Groundhog Day as Jon Rahm faced the media at the BMW PGA Championship. The burning questions at Wentworth, of course, concerned the uncertain futures of both the Spaniard and LIV Golf – and Rahm once again failed to commit to the beleaguered league.

Golf.title: How to stop sliding during the downswing for better ball striking
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Mark Durland explains why sliding during the downswing hurts your ball striking — and how to fix it. The post How to stop sliding during the downswing for better ball striking appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the most common trends I see among mid-handicap golfers is a tendency to slide through the downswing rather than rotate. This can create several seemingly unrelated problems such as poor driver performance, inconsistent iron compression, a steep angle of attack, and an excessively inside-out club path that produces blocks and over-hooks.

The golf swing is a blend of three forces: vertical, lateral, and rotational. Every golfer uses all three, but problems arise when those forces become unbalanced. For this type of player, there is often too much lateral movement and not enough rotation.

Golf.title: The 2026 PGA Tour's winningest putters show mallets are the new king
Golf.summary: The TaylorMade Spider was again the winningest putter on the PGA Tour, but mallets in general were nearly unbeatable. The post The 2026 PGA Tour’s winningest putters show mallets are the new king appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were to describe the list of PGA Tour winning putters with two words, the first would easily be “mallet.” Across 37 events with 38 winners, only five events by three different pros were won all season by a blade putter. Matt Fitzpatrick won three times with his Bettinardi blade while Tom Kim and Ryan Fox made it a blade sweep in the PGA Tour’s two links golf events, the Scottish Open and Open Championship.

Other than that, every other event this season was won by players using mallet putters. Nine of those players, combining for 13 wins, were using TaylorMade Spider family putters and 11 of them were using the flagship Spider Tour X. The 11 wins for the Spider Tour X shape were more than any other putter brand this season.

Golf.title: Cabot is building a second golf resort in Nova Scotia. Here's what we know

Golf.body:
In 1497, the navigator John Cabot, fresh off explorations of eastern Canada, returned to England to a hero’s welcome. More than 500 years later, a global brand that bears his name is planning a homecoming of a different kind.

Cabot, the prominent golf and real-estate developer with a portfolio of marquee properties around the world, on Monday announced its latest project: Cabot Wilds, a destination resort in Nova Scotia anchored by an 18-hole course from Canadian architect Jeff Mingay, set to open in late 2027. The project is being developed in partnership with Canadian businessman John Bragg, a longtime Cabot investor who recently increased his stake in the company.

Golf.body:
The wheels on the bus go round and round. The questions about the bus keep coming, too. The U.S. team bus at the Solheim Cup, that is. They first arose on Saturday evening in the Netherlands, when Team USA erupted in sudsy celebration of Jennifer Kupcho’s fourball heroics, which had turned around the day’s last match. What had looked like a sure deficit heading into Sunday was now deadlocked, and the Americans were in a festive mood.

Out came beers on the team bus. As videos of the moment swirled on social media, so did questions — and criticism — from online commentators. Wasn’t it too early to celebrate? How did the optics look? Might the boozy antics lead to a letdown? Provide the Europeans with extra motivation?

Golf.title: Shane Lowry wins second Irish Open title in record-setting fashion
Golf.summary: Shane Lowry fired a final-round 63 to win his second career Irish Open by a record margin — 17 years after his first. The post Shane Lowry wins second Irish Open title in record-setting fashion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Sunday marked a career that’s come full circle for Irishman Shane Lowry. The 39-year-old notched his fifth career DP World Tour victory at the Amgen Irish Open, held at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg on the Emerald Isle’s southwest coast.

The victory was Lowry’s second Irish Open win, 17 years after he claimed his first Irish Open title as an amateur in 2019. Ten years later, in 2019, Lowry won his maiden major championship at Royal Portrush.

Golf.title: Europe reclaims Solheim Cup with dominant Sunday singles performance
Golf.summary: Europe needed 6.5 points from Sunday singles to wrest the Solheim Cup back from the Americans. They managed that — and then some. The post Europe reclaims Solheim Cup with dominant Sunday singles performance appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Jennifer Kupcho drained two birdie bombs to flip her and Lindy Duncan’s four-ball match against Europe’s Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier and tie the Solheim Cup score at 8-8 on Saturday evening, the giddy celebrations that ensued seemed to direct the momentum firmly to the Americans’ corner.

But, on Sunday, a commanding performance by the Europeans in singles stymied the Americans’ charge at Bernardus Golf, as Europe secured the necessary points to reclaim the Cup with three matches still undecided on the course.

Golf.title: Does the Presidents Cup need to change its points structure? | Subpar
Golf.summary: Tour veteran Brendon de Jonge, a past member of the International Presidents Cup team, joined Subpar to discuss the biennial event and more. The post Does the Presidents Cup need to change its points structure? | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Walker Cup wrapped up last week, the Solheim Cup finishes this weekend and next up on the team-event schedule is the Presidents Cup, which gets underway in less than two weeks at Medinah Country Club outside of Chicago.

The Americans will be heavily favored once again, and they lead the all-time series 13-1-1. The tie came in 2003, and the International team’s only win was in 1998. It’s been two decades of U.S. dominance, as the Americans have won the last 10, and three of the last four wins have been by five points or more.

Golf.title: Here's where the next Solheim Cup will be played in 2028
Golf.summary: As the 2026 Solheim Cup finishes up in the Netherlands, next up will be 2028 in the United States. Here's a look at past and future venues. The post Here’s where the next Solheim Cup will be played in 2028 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The 2026 Solheim Cup finishes this weekend in the Netherlands, which means you’ll have to wait two more years before the next iteration of the biennial event arrives. Although in 2028 it returns to the U.S.

Next up is Valhalla Golf Club in Louisville, Ky., to host the 21st playing of the Solheim Cup come Sept. 8-10, 2028. Valhalla is no stranger to golf’s marquee events. It’s hosted four PGA Championships, two Senior PGA Championships and the 2008 Ryder Cup. It most recently hosted the 2024 PGA, which was won by Xander Schauffele but perhaps most remembered for the bizarre arrest of World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler.

Golf.title: After posting his most lucrative season to date, Jake Knapp has sights set on majors
Golf.summary: Nine top-25 finishes made 2026 Jake Knapp's most lucrative Tour season to date. But the 32-year-old is focusing on loftier goals. The post After posting his most lucrative season to date, Jake Knapp has sights set on majors appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
At 32, he’s not your typical “new” PGA Tour star, but he definitely played like one this season. Dylan Dethier: You played some really good golf in 2026 — 11th or better in seven of your first eight starts this season, including the Masters. What does it feel like to be on a run like that?

Jake Knapp: I mean, obviously it feels good. It doesn’t feel, like, crazy different; it’s not like I’m hitting it exactly where I want to on every shot or making every putt or chipping in all the time. I just think I did a job good this offseason analyzing what areas I could really benefit from the most — maximizing my practice time, locking in on ball striking — and seeing improvement has been great. Obviously, when you’re playing well, you want to try to take advantage and win, but when you put yourself in contention as often as you can that’s uplifting too. Because golf is golf; you’re going to have some weird stuff happen. But when it does you know that it’s, like, Hey, I’m playing fine. That’s the sign, really, that your work is kind of coming to fruition and then you see it show up with results.

Golf.title: Inspired Lowry takes four-shot lead into final day
Golf.summary: Shane Lowry produces an inspired display on the greens to take a four-shot lead into the final round of the Irish Open and close in on his first individual win since 2022.
Golf.body:
Shane Lowry produced an inspired display on the greens to take a four-shot lead into the final round of the Irish Open and close in on his first individual win since 2022. The Irishman started the third round three shots clear after shooting a scintillating course-record 62 on Friday at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare.

Despite being caught by Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry one-putted every green on the back nine in a five-under 65 to maintain control of the tournament. "I'm normally the one watching other people do it, so why not me sometimes," Lowry said when asked about his joy on the greens.

Golf.title: Jennifer Kupcho's late heroics flip the script at Solheim Cup
Golf.summary: At the Solheim Cup Saturday, 2 birdie bombs by Jennifer Kupcho helped tie the match at 8-8 heading into Sunday singles. The post Jennifer Kupcho’s late heroics flip the script at Solheim Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Jennifer Kupcho cupped a hand to her ear toward the grandstands, then raised a finger to her lips to shush the gallery further. The quiet that fell over the crowd stood in stark contrast to the pyrotechnics Kupcho had just provided on a taut Saturday at the Solheim Cup. Paired with Lindy Duncan and down a hole with two to play, Kupcho birdied both 17 and 18, completing a remarkable comeback and stealing a point from Céline Boutier and Carlota Ciganda.

The win gave the Americans a 3-1 edge in the afternoon fourballs and brought the competition level heading into Sunday singles, with the teams tied 8-8. “I don’t know, walking up to the green, honestly, like, I just thought, like, OK, during all these practice rounds, I’d just get up and whack it,” Kupcho said. “So, yeah, really didn’t read it. I was, like, all right, we’ll just give it a run, make sure we get it there, but what the heck it went in. That was insane.”

Well over a year after Badminton Wales released its ‘Can You Manage?’ campaign that challenged common perceptions about Para badminton athletes, the message has lost none of its resonance.

Conceived to reframe Para badminton players as high-performance competitors rather than solely as participants or figures who inspire, the video campaign won the Promotion Award at the BWF Member Association Awards in June 2026.

I grew up in a lower middle class family. I first played badminton at the age of 12 in a sports centre called Agustín Millán Viveros. However, due to family reasons, we moved to Michoacán, and I stopped playing badminton for many years. It was 13 years later that badminton returned to my life when I entered university.

Badminton.title: Korean Women Dominate Early At BWF China Masters
Badminton.summary: Korean Women Dominate Early At BWF China Masters Evrim Ağacı
Badminton.body:
The 2026 BWF China Masters in Shenzhen, China, kicked off with a bang as Korean women’s singles shuttlers An Se-young, Kim Ga-eun, and Shim Yu-jin all stormed into the round of 16, each delivering commanding performances in their opening matches. The tournament, a Super 750 event running from September 1 to September 6, has already seen its share of drama and upsets, with Korea’s top women shining while the country’s leading men’s doubles pair suffered a shock early exit.

World number one An Se-young wasted no time in asserting her dominance. Facing Taiwan’s Lin Xiang-ti in the round of 32, An put on a clinic, winning 2-0 (21-11, 21-3) in just 33 minutes. The match saw An steadily pull away, building momentum with a series of runs—she broke a 9-8 deadlock in the first game with four straight points and then sealed the deal in the second with relentless attacking play, surging to an 11-1 lead and never looking back. It was another display of the form that saw her claim a flawless victory at last month’s World Championships in New Delhi, where she didn’t drop a single game en route to the title.

Badminton.title: BWF Regional Coalition Updates - September 2026
Badminton.summary: BWF Regional Coalition Updates - September 2026 Utah State University
Badminton.body:
September Newsletter for the Utah Women & Leadership Project at Utah State University. In the Bolder Way Forward (BWF) Framework, grassroots is key to making long-term societal change, and that means getting the message to every community, neighborhood, and family in Utah. Leaders and supporters across Utah ensure this happens. The following are quarterly updates for each BWF Region. Please click on the individual County Coalition webpages (linked below) to learn more.

Daggett, Duchesne, Summit, Uintah and Wasatch Counties continue to foster meaningful collaboration, strengthen community partnerships, and advance local efforts across the Uintah Basin, Wasatch, and Summit County regions. With direction from BWF’s Movement-Wide Awareness Campaigns, each coalition creates unique social media posts as they share UWLP and BWF posts. As local leadership transitions, the Daggett, Duchesne and Uintah coalition is seeking new community leads and working to restart the Lunch and Learn series now that the school year is underway. Wasatch County leaders are working with local public radio station KPCW to gather community perspectives for a series of pieces and online articles examining women’s experiences with domestic violence and navigating the judicial system. They are working with partners, including the Peace House, to bring an event to Wasatch County in October, recognizing Domestic Violence Awareness month. Summit County leaders attended the June workshop “Your Strengths, Utah’s Future: Building a State Where All Can Thrive” where networking opportunities arose. They continue to work to rebuild engagement amongst the coalition members, reconnecting with community partners while they identify opportunities to strengthen participation and restore momentum. To get involved, contact Jayden Sillert, UWLP East Central Regional Coordinator.

Badminton.title: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches
Badminton.summary: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches BWF
Badminton.body:
August was a good month for the conservation of badminton heritage, with two museums opening in Europe just a day apart – one in Germany, the other in Denmark. Quite significantly, they are the first badminton museums in either country.

Badminton Museum Bonn, located in the premises of Badminton Club Beuel (Germany’s biggest club), showcases the personal collection of former players and history enthusiasts Helga and Roland Maywald, and opened on 29 August. While most badminton museums celebrate the competition aspect of the sport (players, tournaments), the Maywalds’ collection is devoted to preserving badminton’s presence in the everyday lives of people over the past few centuries, through historical artefacts such as porcelain figurines, postcards, paintings, etc.

Badminton.title: ‘I Want to be a Legend’
Badminton.summary: ‘I Want to be a Legend’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Winning, and making history along the way, has become almost routine for An Se Young. The world No.1 has already collected seven individual titles this season, putting her on course to eclipse the record-equalling 11 she won last year. Yet, she heads into next week’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with her focus firmly on the next match rather than the numbers piling up behind her.

“Records make you a legend. I want to be a legend in badminton,” An said. “But also, they mean you keep improving yourself. So it makes me more motivated. “I always think I can improve further because my rivals could catch up and overtake me. I never take any match for granted.”

Badminton.title: Badminton duo win in Vietnam
Badminton.summary: Badminton duo win in Vietnam Taipei Times
Badminton.body:
Taiwan’s Chen Zhi-ray and Lin Yu-chieh won the men’s doubles final at the Yonex-Sunrise Vietnam Open badminton tournament on Sunday, dispatching their Singaporean opponents in 27 minutes in back-to-back games.

Chen and Lin defeated Singapore’s Terry Hee and Howin Wong at the Badminton World Federation (BWF) Super 100 event 21-14, 21-12 at the Nguyen Du Club in Ho Chi Minh City. The victory is the duo’s first BWF Tour event win since they paired up in 2024.

Badminton.title: Japan Para: Rich Haul for Peru; Jauregui Excels
Badminton.summary: Japan Para: Rich Haul for Peru; Jauregui Excels BWF
Badminton.body:
Peru finished strong at the Japan Para Badminton International 2026, with Pilar Jauregui winning two gold medals. The Wheelchair (WH2) player partnered Malaysia’s Muhammad Ikhwan Ramli to the mixed doubles (WH1-WH2) gold as they won all their group matches.

Jaurequi then made the WH2 women’s singles final where she beat Turkiye’s Emine Seckin 13-21 21-8 21-15. Jaurequi’s compatriot Rubi Fernandez won the women’s singles Short Stature (SH6) gold, beating another Turkiye player, Elif Dokuzluoglu, 21-12 21-8.

Badminton.title: Behind the Mic, Matsuyama Finds Reprieve
Badminton.summary: Behind the Mic, Matsuyama Finds Reprieve BWF
Badminton.body:
Nami Matsuyama has spent years experiencing the Japan Open from the court. This year, she saw it from behind the microphone. Recovering from ACL surgery, the doubles specialist made an unexpected Japan Open debut in a new role, joining broadcaster J Sports as a colour commentator for the mixed doubles match featuring her regular partner Hiroki Midorikawa and Olympic champion Misaki Matsutomo.

For Matsuyama, the assignment was the realisation of a long-held ambition and a chance to discover a different side of the sport she knows so well. “This is one of my dreams,” she said. “I just wanted to try this and today I did it.”

Competitor News.title: Deutsche Bank links up with Singapore Open in four-year title partnership
Competitor News.summary: Deutsche Bank links up with Singapore Open in four-year title partnership sportsmintmedia.com
Competitor News.body:
Deutsche Bank has signed a multi-year agreement to become the title partner of the Singapore Open through 2029, giving the historic Asian golf tournament a major international financial-services brand as it returns to the DP World Tour schedule in 2027.

The tournament will be renamed the Deutsche Bank Singapore Open from next season and will be played at Sentosa Golf Club’s The Serapong course from April 15–18, 2027. The event will be jointly sanctioned by the DP World Tour and Asian Tour and will form part of the DP World Tour’s 2027 Asian Swing and the opening phase of the Race to Dubai.

Competitor News.title: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership
Competitor News.summary: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership Golf Industry Asia
Competitor News.body:
The Deutsche Bank Singapore Open will return to Sentosa Golf Club’s Serapong course from 15–18 April 2027 as a co-sanctioned event between the DP World Tour and Asian Tour. The announcement confirms Sentosa’s continued status as one of Asia’s leading championship venues. Earlier in 2026, the club hosted three major championships, including the Singapore Open, within an eight-week window. The course has long been recognised for its championship conditioning, Tournament Ready 365 (TR365) agronomy programme and industry-leading sustainability practices.

The Singapore Open first came to The Serapong on the Asian Tour in 2005, when Adam Scott claimed the first of his three titles there. Between 2009 and 2012 the event was co-sanctioned by the European Tour (now DP World Tour) and Asian Tour. After a four-year absence, the tournament returned to Sentosa in April 2026.
